candidates.original_title: The relationship between selected immediacy behaviors and cognitive learning
candidates.description: Instructor nonverbal immediacy behaviors are positively related to students' cognitive learning, including perceived learning and learning loss.
candidates.citation_sentence: This study replicated [15] study on nonverbal immediacy and cognitive learning (H1b), with statistically significant relationships (p < .01) between nonverbal immediacy and learning loss (r = -.49), nonverbal immediacy and perceived learning (r = .46), as well as between all of the individual nonverbal immediacy behaviors and both learning loss (r ranging from -.24 to -.44) 2 and perceived learning (r ranging from .28 to .41).
candidates.notes: The paper identifies the original through numbered citation [15]; the sentence does not state the original authors or year in author-year form. The replication used more diverse institutions and modified measurement procedures.

candidates.original_title: The relationship of teacher clarity and immediacy with student state receiver apprehension, affect, and cognitive learning
candidates.description: Instructor clarity is positively related to students' cognitive learning.
candidates.citation_sentence: This project seeks to reexamine the relationships proposed in [19], [4][4][15] foundational studies to identify the relationships among immediacy behaviors, clarity, humor, perceived immediacy, and student cognitive learning.
candidates.notes: The paper identifies the original through numbered citation [4]; the citation sentence does not state the original authors or year in author-year form. Cognitive learning was assessed using multiple learning measures; these are treated as one replicated cognitive-learning effect rather than separate entries. The replication found statistically significant relationships in the expected direction, with measurement-validity caveats.
